title: Long noncoding RNA LIRIL2R modulates FOXP3 levels and suppressive function of human CD4+ regulatory T cells by regulating IL2RA
projectDescription: Long non-coding RNA, LIRIL2R was identified and confirmed to be differentially expressed in regulatory T cells by RNAseq. A role of LIRIL2R was studied in iTreg cells using multiple approaches. Data independent analysis proteomics revealed effects of LIRIL2R knock down in Treg cells. Loss of Treg signature proteins upon LIRIL2R knock down signified the its role  in iTreg cell development and function.
sampleProcessingProtocol: A cell pellet was lysed in a lysis buffer (5% SDS in 50 mM TRIS-HCl, pH 7.6) at room temperature. To shear the DNA and reduce the lysate viscosity, the samples were incubated with Benzonase for 10 min. The extract was heated at 95 °C for 5 min and clarified by centrifugation at 13,000 x g for 10 min. Protein concentration was measured by DC assay. Then, dithiothreitol (DTT) (stock solution of 0.5M in 50 mM TRIS-HCl) was added to a final concentration of 10 mM. Iodoacetamide (IAA) (stock solution of 1M in in 50 mM TRIS-HCl) was added to a final concentration of 20 mM. Following incubation for 30 min in the dark, the lysate was digested by Suspension Trapping (STrap) (Protifi, Huntington, NY) method. Briefly, the alkylated proteins were first acidified by phosphoric acid to a final concentration of 1.2 % and then mixed with 6 volumes of binding buffer (90% methanol, 100 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate, TEAB, pH 7.1). The sample was vortexed and then loaded onto the STrap column. Following a quick centrifugation at 4000 x g for 1–2 min, the filter was washed 2–3 times with 160 μL binding buffer, and proteins were subjected to overnight digestion with 10 μg of MS-grade trypsin (in 50 μL of 50 mM TRIS-HCl) at 37 °C. The digested peptides were recovered by stepwise elution with 50 μL of 50 mM TRIS-HCl, 50 μL of 0.2% formic acid/water, and 50 μL of 50% acetonitrile/50% water. Peptide elutions were pooled and dried in SpeedVac.
dataProcessingProtocol: The dried peptides were reconstituted in formic acid/acetonitrile mixture, and an amount corresponding to 1000 ng was analysed using EasynLC 1200 coupled to Orbitrap Fusion™ Lumos™ mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). The peptides were then loaded onto a pre column (20 x 0.1 mm), followed by separation over a 120 min gradient on 75 µm x 15 cm analytical column (both in-house packed with 3 µm Reprosil C18; Dr Maisch GmbH). The peptides were eluted with a gradient from 5 to 21 % B phase in 62 min then to 36 % B in 48 min then to 100 % B in 5 min and maintaining it for 5 more minutes, at flow rate of 300 nL/min. The mobile phase compositions were, water with 0.1 % formic acid (A) and 80 % acetonitrile 0.1 % formic acid (B). The temperature of the column was maintained at 60 ⁰C using a column oven. A Data Independent Analysis was performed on positive mode with MS resolution of 120K, MS scan range (m/z) of 395-1005, AGC target of 700000, cycle time of 3 sec and maximum injection time of 50 ms. A high-field asymmetric ion mobility spectrometer (FAIMS) with two compensation voltages of -50 V and -70 V was applied. The data was acquired with 30 variable mass windows for each scan cycle. The MS/MS scan range (m/z) was set to 180-2000, loop control to 3, normalized collision energy to 28 %, Orbitrap resolution to 30K, maximum injection time of 52 ms and AGC target to 1000000. The raw files were converted to .htrms files using htrms converter and directDIA database search was performed using Spectronaut (v15). Trypsin was selected as the digestion enzyme. Carbamidomethylation was selected as a fixed modification, and methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation were selected as variable modifications. FDRs was set to 0.01.
